newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - July 9.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - July 9.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

Gold prices bounced somewhat on overnight commodity markets for the first time since the Reserve Bank of Australia announced it had sold off 167 tonnes of gold. Bullion rose to close in New York at US$320.05 an ounce and fixed in London at US$320.80 an ounce from US$318 on Tuesday.

News Corp Ltd is trying to sell its 40 percent stake in multi-media group PMP Communiciations Ltd for A$3.20 a share through Were Stockbroking, The Australian and The Sydney Morning Herald newspapers reported on Wednesday. PMP said later on Wednesday it had received no formal notification of a change of shareholding but would not comment on whether it had received informal notification.

News Corp said Tuesday the company was exploring a possible joint venture with prospective partners for its HarperCollins book publishing business, including selling a stake in the unit. The spokesman said the talks were preliminary. News Corp chairman Rupert Murdoch, in a Wall Street Journal interview Tuesday, denied rumors that News Corp wants to sell all of HarperCollins.

RGC Ltd assured shareholder on Tuesday that plans to buy and develop a US$300 million gold/copper project in Peru would not require any equity raising. Earlier, RGC announced it had agreed to buy the Cerro Corona project in the Andes in Northern Peru for a US$2 million deposit and a one-off payment of US$34 million after due diligence or US$37 million in three payments over three years.

Energy Resources of Australia Ltd, which mines about 7.5 percent of the world's market for uranium, said on Tuesday low metal prices would weigh on profits in the 1996-97 year ended-June 30. "This year we won't repeat last year's figure," ERA chief executive Phillip Shirvington told reporters at the company's Ranger mine.

Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd said on Tuesday that while it expected to be able to fully frank its 1997 final dividend, future franking would depend on its future profit mix. "There may be limits on franking capacity going forward, depending on the balance between Australia and offshore profits.," the bank said in a statement.
Brambles Industries Ltd said on Tuesday it had acquired 100 percent of the CHEP New Zealand pallet rental business for an undisclosed sum.

Gold miner Australian Resources ltd said on tuesday recent exploration had made it confident of an increase in its reserve and resource inventory. The company said recent intersections at its Gidgee project in Western Australia had included 18 metres averaging 52 grams per tonne gold (g/t), 4.4 metres at 71.41 g/t, and nine metres at 48.01 g/t.
